title: Stability Sentinel playlist and telemetry traffic sim plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact, repeatable playbook for (1) running a synthetic-traffic rehearsal before a staged release lane, (2) mapping telemetry signals to go/no-go gates, and (3) drafting the release notes that will be posted after stabilization. Intended audience: release engineers, SRE on-call, owners for serving-runtime, and product owners for the release window.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to any deployment that touches the serving runtime (model server changes, kernel updates, batching/queueing changes, routing/policy updates).
- Not a replacement for safety lane cutover or legal/compliance signoffs. Keep the privacy review checklist separately.
- We assume availability of canary clusters (region-control and region-canary) and ability to inject synthetic traffic at the edge and at the request router level.

High-level schedule (week-of cadence for a medium-risk rollout):
- Day -7: Kickoff and telemetry smoke (owners assigned, test harness booked)
- Day -4: Baseline capture (24h of production sampling for key metrics)
- Day -2: Synthetic traffic run 1 (functional validation, low qps)
- Day -1: Synthetic traffic run 2 (scale to target qps for warm-cache behavior)
- Release day: Canary open for 2–6 hours, monitor gates continously, proceed to lane progression if green
- +24h: Post-rollout regression run and notes draft

Checklist: pre-sim (owners and artifacts)
- Owner: release lead (primary) and SRE (secondary). Names pinned in calendar invite.
- Confirm canary cluster snapshot and identical config to prod (env vars, kernel flags) — infra PR link and diff attached.
- Ensure feature flags for traffic split are set with a manual override. Document flag name and safe-default.
- Verify data retention/PII masking for synthetic traces (use anonymized user IDs and deterministic seeds).
- Reserve observability workspace: dashboards pinned for the run, tracing sampling increased to 100% for 30m windows.
- Validate synthetic traffic runner (version tag + replay scripts) and store seed/config in release artifact.

Synthetic traffic scenarios (priority order)
1) Baseline replay: 10–15% of peak qps using production traces sampled from Day -4. Goal: ensure no regressions in p95/p99 latency or error spike.
2) Cold-start churn: bursty new session starts to exercise model load paths, KV cache filling. Monitor cold-start latency and GPU memory churn.
3) Long context stream: sustained long-session requests (seq len > typical) to exercise attention kernel selection and KV eviction heuristics.
4) Error amplification: inject 5% malformed requests to validate validation layer and rate-limiter behaviour.
5) Gradual scale to target canary proportion (ramp 0.1% -> 5% -> 25% of lane) verifying linearity in latency/cost.

Telemetry signal catalog and go/no-go thresholds (primary signals first)
- API error rate (5xx) — threshold: <0.2% absolute increase over baseline in the canary cluster for 30m.
- Client-visible latencies: p50/p95/p99 — threshold: p95 increase <10% over baseline; p99 <20% for persistent 30m window.
- Inference rejection/validation errors — threshold: <0.1% new increase.
- GPU memory pressure / OOM events — threshold: zero OOMs; any OOM event => immediate rollback.
- Queue length and request wait time — threshold: median queue < x ms (define per-run, use baseline). Spike in queue length + tail latency => investigate.
- Cost delta (tokens/sec * effective CPU/GPU time): allow short transient increases during cache warmup; sustained >15% increase over baseline => rollback consideration.
- Traces: error spans per minute compared to baseline; new stack frames from recent changes flagged as high priority.

Automated gating rules (what the automation will enforce)
- If 5xx error rate exceeds threshold for two consecutive 5-minute windows => auto-fallback to prior model/variant.
- If GPU OOM event occurs => immediate circuit-break and rollback.
- If p99 latency exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive 1-minute samples => pause traffic ramp and alert on-call.

Rollback decision tree (short form)
- Severity classification:
  - Sev 1: customer-facing outages, traffic loss, unrecoverable OOMs. Action: immediate rollback to previous stable snapshot and page on-call SRE.
  - Sev 2: degraded latency or error increases that materially impact SLA but not full outage. Action: pause rollout, revert recent infra changes if present, escalate to release lead for decision within 15m.
  - Sev 3: small regressions, non-urgent metric drift. Action: continue monitoring; file follow-up ticket and schedule patch if repeated.

Runbook steps during a detected failure:
1) Freeze traffic ramp (manual flip or automated) and mark canary as quarantined in ticket and status board.
2) Collect artifacts: last 60m traces, p95/p99 distributions, GPU metrics, service logs, kernel selection logs, and the synthetic-run seed.
3) Attempt mitigation: toggle safety fallback (use model-variant B), reduce batch size, or enable degraded routing to lower-cost instance class.
4) If mitigation fails in 10–15m, rollback to previous GA snapshot and start postmortem template.

Post-run release notes draft template (short):
- Summary: short one-liner about the release (what changed and why)
- Scoped changes: list of infra/runtime deltas (kernel change, queueing tweak, model variant)
- Observability highlights: what dashboards we monitored and any important baselines captured
- Impact: if any regressions observed and remedial actions taken
- Rollback history: whether rolled back and which snapshot used
- Follow-ups: tickets created and owners + due dates

Example text (to adapt for final release notes):
"Release X.Y: Batching scheduler update and kernel opt for attention-ops. Canary ramped to 25% in region-us-west on 2026-09-06. No customer-facing errors observed. p95 improved 7% vs baseline; cost-per-token reduced ~3% after warm cache leveled. One transient spike in queue length at minute 42 of canary run; mitigated by reducing max-batch-size from 256 -> 192. No rollback needed. Follow-up: increase tracing on kernel selector for next minor release (OWNER: Priya Singh)."

Open questions and unresolved work:
- Confirm threshold for cost delta that triggers rollback is aligned with product finance (need signoff from Finance: Jeremy Holt).
- Add sanity-check for tokenization regressions (embedding drift) — who owns the test?
- Validate privacy mask for synthetic trace generator across EU regions (legal review).

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Synthetic runner: infra/tools/sim-runner:v1.4 (run: sim-runner --config release-X-Y.json --seed 20260902)
- Dashboards: Observability / Releases / Stability-Sentinel (pinned)
- Trace link pattern: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/{trace_id}

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc intended to be copied into a release-specific checklist. Please review the telemetry thresholds (especially p99) and add comments inline with alternative threshold proposals. If you are an on-call SRE reviewing, please confirm the exact escalation channels and contact rotation to embed in the final runbook.

Signed-off-by: Ava Chen (release engineering)
